verdict.rationale: PagerDuty documents API versioning. A REST API versioning page describes a version header that pins responses to a specified API version, the Events API is explicitly v2, and V3 webhooks come with a migration guide from previous versions. No evidence shows a formal deprecation policy, such as sunset timelines or notice periods. The community complaint about v1/v2 key confusion concerns telling keys apart, not whether versioning exists, so it does not create a dispute. missing for 10: a documented deprecation/sunset policy with timelines, and independent corroboration of version stability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: Any request made using this header will respond with the specified API version, regardless of the authentication token used.
The Events API v2 is a highly reliable, highly available **asynchronous API**
V3 webhooks provide the foundation for the future of PagerDuty webhooks. When compared with previous versions, they provide additional event types
please follow our [migration guide](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/webhooks#migration-guide) or use our [migration script]
